channel.title: Down to Earth - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Down to Earth (downtoearth.org.in)

item.title: Daily Court Digest: Major environment orders (February 13, 2026)
item.description: The Supreme Court mandates compliance with the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, urging authorities to establish necessary infrastructure. Meanwhile, the NGT orders demarcation of Madhya Pradesh wetlands to protect them, emphasizing coordination among departments for effective implementation.

item.title: Unmasking the methane myth: Why India’s cows emit far less than global estimates
item.description: India's livestock methane emissions are overestimated due to generalized IPCC methods. Accurate, region-specific data is needed for effective mitigation and economic benefits through carbon credits.

item.title: Aravallis, the mountain range that defines itself
item.description: The Aravalli mountain range, one of the world's oldest, faces a definitional debate that could impact legal protections and mining activities. Experts argue that height-based criteria overlook its ancient geological continuity, risking fragmentation of its ecological and structural integrity.

item.title: Summer from February? First 15 days see temperatures soaring across India
item.description: India faces an early summer in February 2026, with temperatures soaring above normal in 27 cities, threatening Rabi crops. The lack of rain and snow exacerbates the situation, impacting food security and agriculture, particularly in North India.

item.title: ‘No good ground to interfere’: NGT approves Andaman-Nicobar port project, dismisses all petitions
item.description: The NGT has approved the Andaman-Nicobar port project, dismissing petitions citing ecological concerns. The tribunal emphasized compliance with environmental and coastal regulations, allowing the project to proceed with conditions for coral conservation and strategic importance.

item.title: Rajasthan farmers fear wheat losses as February temperatures surge 5-6°C above normal
item.description: Rajasthan farmers are worried as February temperatures rise 5-6°C above normal, threatening wheat crops in the milky stage. Canal water shortages exacerbate the situation, with potential yield losses reminiscent of 2022. Scientists attribute the volatility to climate change.

item.title: A new diagnosis of ‘profound autism’ is on the cards. Here’s what could change
item.description: The proposed 'profound autism' category aims to better support autistic individuals with significant needs, but concerns arise over age thresholds and funding alignment. The study reveals 24% of children may meet the criteria, highlighting the need for tailored support and inclusive language.

item.title: Economists and environmental scientists see the world differently — here’s why that matters
item.description: Economists and environmental scientists differ in their views on environmental issues, leading to varied solutions. Economists favor market-based approaches, while scientists advocate for systemic changes. This divergence stems from their distinct perceptions.

item.title: Researchers improve method to generate clean energy from human urine
item.description: Researchers have enhanced a method to convert human urine into electricity, offering a cost-effective solution for wastewater treatment and renewable energy. By using microbial fuel cells with higher urine concentrations, they achieved improved electricity output and pollutant removal.
